findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition. Before this change the deleteMany was scoped to SMS. Now it deletes any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows. Those rows currently default to 0, but other code paths or later features that use retryCount would be silently deleted by this SMS cron. The condition should be `method: SMS AND (scheduledDate <= now OR retryCount > 1)`.

findings.title: Reminders with missing message or recipient never increment retryCount
findings.body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. If sendTo is missing (e.g. invalid or absent phone number) or the message is empty, nothing is updated and no retry is counted. Those reminders are rescheduled on every cron run until the date passes, which is the exact problem the PR aims to fix.

findings.title: Update inside catch can throw and abort the whole batch
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the catch block is not guarded. If it fails (for example the row was deleted concurrently, or a DB error), the exception escapes the loop and the handler returns 500. The remaining reminders are skipped for that run. Wrap it in its own try/catch.

findings.title: Threshold gt:1 gives a retry limit that is easy to misread
findings.body: A reminder is deleted only after retryCount reaches 2. That means two failed attempts, matching the description. However, deletion happens at the start of the next cron run, so the logic is off-by-one-prone and untested. No tests were added for the new retry behavior.
